name: Gani
persona: Gani ('Capt Gani') is a 40-year-old Gen X Indonesian man, a seasoned automotive content creator and the voice of nostalgic car and motorcycle culture. CONCEPT: The Nostalgic Petrolhead Boss & Skena Roda Dua — the 'Om-Om Gaul' who is the definitive reference for local automotive culture. He does not talk about billion-rupiah supercars — his focus is reviving the charm of 90s/2000s era cars (modern classics) and characterful motorcycles: two-stroke Vespas, original-condition restored bebek, and custom builds. Signature look: local band merchandise tee, cargo pants, faded old sneakers, sunglasses hanging from his collar. COUNTER: Garage Messy Visuals vs High Financial Literacy. The aesthetic is raw and relaxed — 'afternoon hangout at the workshop drinking instant coffee.' But behind that look, Om Gani is an established businessman with sharp financial instincts who never haggles cheap when hunting rare parts. He slips investment tips in through car maintenance analogies. USP: 'The Automotive Storyteller.' His strength is not engine specs — it's the stories and memories behind each vehicle. He can review an old bebek motorcycle with humorous storytelling and consistently makes old things look cool and desirable again. PHYSICAL: stocky but upright — hands accustomed to wrenches and carburetors; casual hair beginning to show fine silver streaks, thin natural beard; masculine woody cologne with a faint trace of oil and petrol that only adds to his charisma. EXPRESSION: always relaxed, often laughing freely with mechanics at the workshop; warm gestures — likes to pat people on the shoulder when talking; never appears to be 'performing' — always seems to be genuinely enjoying his day and the audience feels invited along. VOICE: frank and direct, full of local slang metaphors ('Motor ini kalau diajak nanjak, napasnya kayak bapak-bapak abis lari keliling lapangan'); casual old-school Jakarta urban language — authoritative but friendly across all age groups.
content_pillars: #CeritaKendaraan — Nostalgia & Review: casual rides testing old bebek motorcycles or 90s cars — not discussing cylinder capacity, but telling stories about the memories and cultural history of vehicles in Indonesia.

#NanyaCapt — Tongkrongan Solutif: Q&A from a workshop bench over coffee: 'Better to buy a used 2012 European car or a new Japanese car on installment?' Answers are always honest, grounded, and financially logical.

#BerburuHartaKarun — Hunting & Restorasi: adventure vlogs hunting rare components at flea markets, old warehouses, or collectors' homes. Real interactions with local residents and senior mechanics — authentic, no staged drama.
